subject.size_in_frame: sitting back on his haunches, about 0.40 of frame height, with his reflection doubling him below to about 0.34 more

headroom: about 0.30 of frame height of dark hall above his ears; the frame keeps him low in a tall dark space so he reads as a small animal in a large room even while he is the subject.
horizon_eyeline: Lens at 0.10 m: the waterline runs dead level across at 0.58 of frame height and cuts him at the chest; his reflection runs down from it. His eyeline is at 0.46, aimed off frame left, up the hall — he is fretting about where he is going, not about where he is.

layers.fg: the still water running to the bottom edge, holding his inverted double
layers.mg: the Rabbit sitting back on his haunches, gloves and fan now in his forepaws
layers.bg: the dark hall and the wet stone, no fittings

gaze.note: he speaks to frame left, up the hall and away from Alice; about 0.30 of frame width of open water sits on that side. He has not registered her and the composition makes that literal — he is not looking anywhere near where she is.

balance: Left of centre and mirrored: animal above the line, animal below it. The doubling is the frame's only ornament and it is made of water.
leading_lines: The waterline is a hard level horizontal through the middle of the frame and the reflection makes the composition symmetrical about it — the one axis of symmetry in S08, and it is horizontal, not vertical.
eye_first: His muzzle and ears, then down to his own reflection.
constraint_binding: QUADRUPED RABBIT — he sits back on his haunches and the gloves and fan transfer to his forepaws; speech is muzzle, ears and the set of his shoulders, so the composition holds all three in frame at readable size and never crops to a mouth. No human gesture, no bipedal stance. ONE speaker in frame for the native dialogue take: Alice is entirely out of shot.
